title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 9th District
area: South-central North Carolina, including all of Alamance, Hoke, Moore, and Randolph counties and portions of Chatham, Cumberland, and Guilford counties (most of Fayetteville, home to Fort Bragg).

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Richard Hudson advanced unopposed. Richard Ojeda won a four-way Democratic primary with 41.8% of the vote.

priorities.text: Says job creation depends on a strong education system, a skilled workforce, and a favorable tax and regulatory environment, and points to H.R. 1 (the Working Families Tax Cuts) as delivering on tax-cut promises to small businesses.
priorities.quote: Creating jobs and strengthening our economy are among my top priorities. I believe the formula for job creation includes a strong education system that empowers a skilled workforce and a common sense tax and regulatory environment.

priorities.text: Says the U.S. must maintain the most lethal, agile, and robust military in the world to counter a growing range of national security threats.
priorities.quote: Today, the United States faces a more diverse range of serious threats than at any point in our history. I believe protecting the country from these threats is the first duty of the federal government, which requires the United States to maintain the most lethal, agile, and robust military in the world.

positions.summary: In a June 2022 interview, said gun control does not work while advancing school-safety and mental-health funding as an alternative to Democratic gun legislation.
positions.quote: Gun control doesn't work. If gun control worked, Chicago would be the safest city in America.

record.text: Chairs the Communications and Technology Subcommittee of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce for the 2025-2026 Congress.

candidates.name: Richard Ojeda
candidates.ballotNote: Won the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary with 41.8% of the vote over three challengers.

priorities.text: Wants to tie the minimum wage to the cost of living and exempt the first $45,000 of income from federal income tax.
priorities.quote: One of my top priorities is tackling the affordability crisis by tying the minimum wage to the cost of living so anyone working 40 hours a week earns a true living wage.

priorities.text: Wants to end partisan gerrymandering and pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act.
priorities.quote: Ending partisan gerrymandering is a top priority... We must also pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore federal oversight and stop discriminatory voting changes before they take effect.

priorities.text: Says he entered the race to protect veterans and military families around Fort Bragg after Department of Government Efficiency-driven cuts to VA jobs.
priorities.quote: I got into this race because I watched Richard Hudson stand by while Donald Trump and Elon Musk gutted the VA through DOGE and pushed a bill that cut thousands of VA jobs.

positions.summary: Supports raising the federal minimum wage and tying it to the cost of living.
positions.quote: Raising the federal minimum wage will give families stability and restore dignity to the work that keeps this country alive.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicaid in North Carolina and capping prescription drug costs.
positions.quote: Expand Medicaid in North Carolina and stop federal sabotage by corrupt politicians.

positions.summary: Supports codifying Roe v. Wade and protecting access to abortion, birth control, and reproductive health care.
positions.quote: I will codify Roe v. Wade, protect the right to choose, and defend access to birth control, cancer screenings, and prenatal care.

positions.summary: Wants billionaires to pay more to fund Social Security and opposes cutting benefits or raising the retirement age.
positions.quote: Make billionaires pay their fair share to keep the program strong.

record.text: As a West Virginia state senator, says he helped pass a medical cannabis law and helped secure teacher pay raises following a statewide teachers' strike.
